title: MTO/OTM Closure Calculus, Aspect Equivalence, and Orientation Resolution
summary: Defines a proposed computational foundation in which primitives organize into transient aspects, MTO resolves aspects into persistent RT, OTM decomposes RT into primitives, and subsequent calculation operates on resolved RT objects.

primitive.definition: The irreducible computational element of the RT calculus.

aspect.definition: A temporary admissible organization of primitives participating in MTO resolution.

RT.definition: A resolved relational condition produced by MTO closure.

fundamental_principles.name: Primitive Persistence
fundamental_principles.statement: Primitives persist across MTO and OTM.

fundamental_principles.name: Aspect Transience
fundamental_principles.statement: Aspects exist only during composition and possess no persistent computational identity after closure.

fundamental_principles.name: RT Persistence
fundamental_principles.statement: Resolved RT is the only lawful continuation object after MTO.

fundamental_principles.name: Identity-Destructive Closure
fundamental_principles.statement: MTO closure destroys the identity of all participating aspects.

fundamental_principles.name: Primitive Decomposition
fundamental_principles.statement: OTM decomposes RT directly into primitives rather than reconstructing historical aspect organizations.

closure_axiom.statement: After MTO closure, participating aspect identities cease to exist as computational objects. Only the resolved RT remains active.

continuation_rule.statement: All subsequent calculations operate exclusively on resolved RT objects.

aspect_equivalence.definition: Distinct lawful aspect organizations are biconditional if they resolve to the same RT.
aspect_equivalence.guard: Equivalence under MTO resolution is not structural identity.

otm_behavior.guarantee: Historical aspect organizations are not recovered.
otm_behavior.consequence: New lawful aspect organizations may emerge during subsequent MTO.

orientation_resolution.primitive_cells: Primitive orientation carriers; cells compose into aspects.
orientation_resolution.orientation_array: Temporary organization of aspects representing an orientation field.
orientation_resolution.principle: The orientation field resolves into a single RT and does not persist after closure.

comparison_model.statement: Comparison is the primitive computational operation. Arithmetic expansion does not continue after closure.

computational_consequences: Aspect identity is discarded during closure.
RT becomes the canonical continuation object.
Equivalent aspect organizations form MTO-resolution classes.
OTM is generative rather than historical.
Resolved RT space contains canonical RT objects.
open_research: Formal semantics of aspect equivalence classes.
Canonical admissibility operator for lawful aspect generation.
Recursive RT-field computation using comparison, MTO, and OTM.
capture_limitations: Chat semantic capture preserves the submitted proposal for governed intake; no mathematical truth, theorem status, physical validity, or canonical promotion is asserted.
